rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE BLAME PIE // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Imagine A Pie — Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
2. Share The Slices — In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Check The Whole — Make sure all slices together equal 100.
4. Find Your Slice — Focus only on your true share.
5. Choose Repair — Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Choose Repair be enough.
rituals.potency_stack:

2. At Check The Whole, separate responsibility from punishment.
3. When you reach Choose Repair, choose one action that fits the facts you found. If you remember one thing, make it this: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE LIFE DIRECTION TEST // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Picture — Picture two arrows.
2. Make Room — One shows the next hour if you obey the thought; the other reveals what unfolds over sixty minutes when you make room for it but follow a chosen value.
3. Name Likely — Name the likely behaviour at each arrow’s end.
4. Select Direction — Select by direction, not by mental volume.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Select Direction is your cue to stop.

rituals.title: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
rituals.name: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
rituals.ritual_name: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
rituals.unique_game_move: Start with Close Door. When Choose Next appears, the round is over.
rituals.recognition_cue: Try Close One Door For Thirty Seconds when every option feels too important to choose. It creates just enough space for a different response.
rituals.situation: Try Close One Door For Thirty Seconds when every option feels too important to choose. It creates just enough space for a different response.
rituals.immediate_need: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.challenge: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Perfectionism & performance pressure

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Try Close One Door For Thirty Seconds when every option feels too important to choose. It creates just enough space for a different response.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.

GAME MOVE
Start with Close Door. When Choose Next appears, the round is over.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Close Door — Picture the two leading options. Cross out one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
2. Read Protest — Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Reopen Choice — Uncross the option. Repeat once with the other door closed so both reactions receive the same test.
4. Choose Next — Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.

⚡ END MOVE — Choose Next. No second lap.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Just before you start Close Door, notice one sound in the room before continuing.
2. At Reopen Choice, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Choose Next, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Your takeaway: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.

rituals.plain:
CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS

TRIGGER
Perfectionism & performance pressure

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Try Close One Door For Thirty Seconds when every option feels too important to choose. It creates just enough space for a different response.

GOAL
A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.

GAME MOVE
Start with Close Door. When Choose Next appears, the round is over.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Close Door — Picture the two leading options. Cross out one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
2. Read Protest — Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Reopen Choice — Uncross the option. Repeat once with the other door closed so both reactions receive the same test.
4. Choose Next — Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.

⚡ END MOVE — Choose Next. No second lap.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Just before you start Close Door, notice one sound in the room before continuing.
2. At Reopen Choice, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Choose Next, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Your takeaway: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
Choose Next becomes possible without giving the reaction another full round.

📸 MY RESULT
“I just found a next choice without solving my whole future.”

FORMULA FLOW
Close Door → Read Protest → Reopen Choice → Choose Next

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Some solutions survive only because their costs stay hidden.

GAME MOVE
Begin where it says Use Control; stop the moment you complete Choose Experiment.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE CONTROL GRAVEYARD // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Use Control — Name everything used to control the feeling: checking, avoiding, numbing, arguing, reassurance, overworking.
2. Picture Short — Beside each, Picture the short-term payoff and the six-month bill.
3. Focus On Costs — Focus on any method whose bill exceeds its relief.
4. Choose Experiment — Choose one experiment in not paying that cost today.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Choose Experiment be enough.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Right before the first move, Use Control, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
2. At Focus On Costs, try the opposite possibility for ten seconds.
3. When you reach Choose Experiment, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: Some solutions survive only because their costs stay hidden.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE THIRD VOICE // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Open Voices — Complete three lines.
2. Name Feeling — FEELING SAYS: include its full truth.
3. Name Facts — FACTS SAY: include only verified information.
4. Build Wisdom — WISE RESPONSE: honour the need in the first line and the constraints in the second.
5. Use Wisdom — Read only the third line before acting.

⚡ FINISH — Use Wisdom closes the round.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Defence narrows the world; sense of where you are reopens it.

GAME MOVE
Start at Let Eyes. Stop at Place Attention. Let the middle do the work.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 FINISH THE LOOK // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Let Eyes — Let your eyes move before your head.
2. Scan Left — Slowly scan left, centre, right, behind if safe, and toward an exit.
3. Name Cues — Name present cues of choice, support, and distance from threat.
4. Allow Neck — Allow the neck to follow only within comfort.
5. Place Attention — End by selecting where attention belongs now.

⚡ FINISH — Place Attention closes the round.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Before you begin Let Eyes, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
2. At Name Cues, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Place Attention, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The useful rule here is simple: Defence narrows the world; sense of where you are reopens it.

📸 MY RESULT

rituals.title: TRACK WHAT HOLDS
rituals.name: TRACK WHAT HOLDS
rituals.unique_game_move: Give yourself one clean run: Locate Bodily first, Add Ingredient last.
rituals.recognition_cue: Track What Holds is a tiny mind game for the moment when the urge feels like an instruction.
rituals.situation: Track What Holds is a tiny mind game for the moment when the urge feels like an instruction.
rituals.immediate_need: Support becomes stronger when it receives precise attention.
rituals.challenge: Support becomes stronger when it receives precise attention.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Urges, impulses & cravings

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Track What Holds is a tiny mind game for the moment when the urge feels like an instruction.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Support becomes stronger when it receives precise attention.

GAME MOVE
Give yourself one clean run: Locate Bodily first, Add Ingredient last.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 TRACK WHAT HOLDS // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Locate Bodily — Locate one bodily sign of steadiness—warmth, pressure, uprightness, ease, or a capable impulse.
2. Describe Boundaries — Say its boundaries and changes for twenty seconds.
3. Ask Memory — Ask what memory, person, posture, or environment strengthens it by one degree.
4. Add Ingredient — Add only that ingredient.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Add Ingredient, you are done.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. When you arrive at Locate Bodily, press both feet down for three seconds.
2. At Ask Memory, give the feeling a name without letting it make the decision.
3. When you reach Add Ingredient, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Support becomes stronger when it receives precise attention.

rituals.win_reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
By Add Ingredient, the first reaction is no longer the only move on the table.

TRIGGER

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Track What Holds is a tiny mind game for the moment when the urge feels like an instruction.

GOAL
Support becomes stronger when it receives precise attention.

GAME MOVE
Give yourself one clean run: Locate Bodily first, Add Ingredient last.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 TRACK WHAT HOLDS // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Locate Bodily — Locate one bodily sign of steadiness—warmth, pressure, uprightness, ease, or a capable impulse.
2. Describe Boundaries — Say its boundaries and changes for twenty seconds.
3. Ask Memory — Ask what memory, person, posture, or environment strengthens it by one degree.
4. Add Ingredient — Add only that ingredient.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Add Ingredient, you are done.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. When you arrive at Locate Bodily, press both feet down for three seconds.
2. At Ask Memory, give the feeling a name without letting it make the decision.
3. When you reach Add Ingredient, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Support becomes stronger when it receives precise attention.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
By Add Ingredient, the first reaction is no longer the only move on the table.

📸 MY RESULT
“I had an urge. I didn't have to become it.”

Locate Bodily → Describe Boundaries → Ask Memory → Add Ingredient

🎮 MAP YOUR OPERATING WINDOW // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Imagine Zones — Imagine three zones: TOO HIGH, WORKABLE, TOO LOW.
2. Add Earliest — Add your earliest personal signs in body, speech, attention, and behaviour.
3. Picture Fastest — Beside each outer zone, Picture the fastest safe route toward the middle.
4. Place Others — Place the Imagine a path where others can help recognise it.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Place Others is your cue to stop.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Remove the manager from respiration.

GAME MOVE
Begin where it says Follow Breaths; stop the moment you complete Witness Motion.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 LET BREATH BREATHE YOU // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Follow Breaths — Follow three natural breaths exactly as they occur.
2. Dont Deepen — Do not deepen, slow, count, or improve them.
3. Start — Notice where each begins by itself and where it ends without instruction.
4. Let Body — Between breaths, let the body choose again.
5. Witness Motion — Your only action is witnessing what already knows how to move.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Witness Motion be enough.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Symmetry gives attention a simple crossing.

GAME MOVE
Enter through Pick Requires; leave as soon as you reach Complete Few. One pass is enough.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE EVEN BRIDGE // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

1. Pick Requires — Pick a count that requires no effort.
2. Count Exhale — Inhale for that count, exhale for the same count, and leave any natural pause untouched.
3. Imagine Pair — Imagine each pair forming equal sides of a bridge.
4. Complete Few — Complete a few balanced crossings, then let counting dissolve.

⚡ DONE — Complete Complete Few, then return to your day.

Play the moves, not the whole life story.

4. Complete Few — Complete a few balanced crossings, then let counting dissolve.

⚡ DONE — Complete Complete Few, then return to your day.

1. At the start of Pick Requires, widen your gaze and notice the edges of the room.
2. At Imagine Pair, name the sensation in plain physical words—pressure, heat, tightness, movement.
3. When you reach Complete Few, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep the clean version: Symmetry gives attention a simple crossing.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
A small gap appears between the reaction and what you do at Complete Few.

“I let my breath breathe itself.”

Pick Requires → Count Exhale → Imagine Pair → Complete Few

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 WHAT SURVIVES THREE STATES? // PLAY
Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

1. Picture Appears — Picture what appears in waking, what appears in dreams, and what is absent or inferred in deep sleep.

rituals.game_move: Start with Picture Appears. When Hold Conclusions appears, the round is over.
rituals.how_to_play:
🎮 WHAT SURVIVES THREE STATES? // PLAY
Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

1. Picture Appears — Picture what appears in waking, what appears in dreams, and what is absent or inferred in deep sleep.
2. Ask Claims — Ask which claims of identity remain supported across all three.
3. Hold Conclusions — Hold conclusions lightly; this is an inquiry into ongoing sense, not a demand for belief.

⚡ END MOVE — Hold Conclusions. No second lap.
rituals.power_up_1: Just before you start Picture Appears, notice one sound in the room before continuing.
rituals.power_up_2: At Ask Claims, ask, “What would count as evidence against my first answer?”.
rituals.power_up_3: When you reach Hold Conclusions, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Take this line with you: Compare experience across waking, dreaming, and dreamless sleep.
rituals.win_reward_raw:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
At Hold Conclusions, you have at least one option the first reaction did not show you.

📸 MY RESULT
“I just stopped measuring my whole life against one snapshot.”
rituals.formula_flow_raw: Picture Appears → Ask Claims → Hold Conclusions

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 SAME VALUE, TWO OUTCOMES // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Imagine Action — Imagine the action succeeding.
2. State Governing — State how your governing value behaves next.
3. Imagine Failing — Imagine it failing.
4. State Value — State how the same value responds there.
5. Let Outcome — Let outcome alter strategy, not your ethical centre.

⚡ FINISH — Let Outcome closes the round.

2. At Imagine Failing, try the opposite possibility for ten seconds.
3. When you reach Let Outcome, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The useful rule here is simple: Stability is trained before the verdict arrives.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE SUSTAINABLE MIDDLE // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Rest Review — Review sleep, food, effort, practice, and rest.
2. Find Area — Find the area swinging between too much and too little.
3. Set Middle — Set a middle range you could repeat for two weeks.
4. Choose Smallest — Choose the smallest adjustment that moves into that band today.

⚡ EXIT — Finish Choose Smallest and leave the game there.

rituals.title: EMPTY THE MENTAL COUNTERTOP
rituals.name: EMPTY THE MENTAL COUNTERTOP
rituals.unique_game_move: Start at Question Promise and keep going only until Choose Physical.
rituals.recognition_cue: When your mind is carrying too many things at once, Empty The Mental Countertop makes the invisible part of the pattern easier to catch.
rituals.situation: When your mind is carrying too many things at once, Empty The Mental Countertop makes the invisible part of the pattern easier to catch.
rituals.immediate_need: Short-term attention is not permanent storage.
rituals.challenge: Short-term attention is not permanent storage.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Attention & cognitive overload

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
When your mind is carrying too many things at once, Empty The Mental Countertop makes the invisible part of the pattern easier to catch.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Short-term attention is not permanent storage.

GAME MOVE
Start at Question Promise and keep going only until Choose Physical.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 EMPTY THE MENTAL COUNTERTOP // PLAY
One pass is enough. Follow what is written.

1. Question Promise — Catch every task, question, promise, and loose obligation into one trusted place.
2. Dont Organise — Do not organise while emptying.
3. Sort Entries — When the mind offers silence, sort entries into do, schedule, delegate, reference, or delete.
4. Choose Physical — Choose only the first physical action.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Choose Physical is your cue to stop.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. As you enter Question Promise, feel where your body is supported for one moment.
2. At Sort Entries, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Choose Physical, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Let this be the line you keep: Short-term attention is not permanent storage.

rituals.plain:
EMPTY THE MENTAL COUNTERTOP

TRIGGER
Attention & cognitive overload

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
When your mind is carrying too many things at once, Empty The Mental Countertop makes the invisible part of the pattern easier to catch.

GOAL
Short-term attention is not permanent storage.

GAME MOVE
Start at Question Promise and keep going only until Choose Physical.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 EMPTY THE MENTAL COUNTERTOP // PLAY
One pass is enough. Follow what is written.

1. Question Promise — Catch every task, question, promise, and loose obligation into one trusted place.
2. Dont Organise — Do not organise while emptying.
3. Sort Entries — When the mind offers silence, sort entries into do, schedule, delegate, reference, or delete.
4. Choose Physical — Choose only the first physical action.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Choose Physical is your cue to stop.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. As you enter Question Promise, feel where your body is supported for one moment.
2. At Sort Entries, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Choose Physical, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Let this be the line you keep: Short-term attention is not permanent storage.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You reach Choose Physical without having to solve the entire situation.

📸 MY RESULT
“I stopped carrying everything at the same time.”

FORMULA FLOW
Question Promise → Dont Organise → Sort Entries → Choose Physical

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE REQUEST SPINE // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Describe Situation — Say the visible situation.
2. Express Impact — Express its impact.
3. Assert Request — Assert the exact request or no.
4. Reinforce Cooperation — Reinforce why cooperation helps.

rituals.ritual_name: IMPACT IS KNOWN; MOTIVE IS PENDING
rituals.unique_game_move: Move through the sequence once, from Dont Know to Leave Motive.
rituals.recognition_cue: Impact Is Known; Motive Is Pending catches the moment when not knowing feels like something you must fix immediately and gives you another route.
rituals.situation: Impact Is Known; Motive Is Pending catches the moment when not knowing feels like something you must fix immediately and gives you another route.
rituals.immediate_need: Do not let mind-reading erase visible harm.
rituals.challenge: Do not let mind-reading erase visible harm.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Uncertainty & reassurance seeking

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
Impact Is Known; Motive Is Pending catches the moment when not knowing feels like something you must fix immediately and gives you another route.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Do not let mind-reading erase visible harm.

GAME MOVE
Move through the sequence once, from Dont Know to Leave Motive.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 IMPACT IS KNOWN; MOTIVE IS PENDING // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Dont Know — Picture three separate statements: what they did; what effect it had; what you do not know about intention.
2. Base — Base your next boundary on behaviour and impact.
3. Leave Motive — Leave motive open until reliable evidence or direct communication updates it.

⚡ FINISH — Leave Motive closes the round.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Before you begin Dont Know, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
2. At Base, try the opposite possibility for ten seconds.
3. When you reach Leave Motive, choose one action that fits the facts you found. If you remember one thing, make it this: Do not let mind-reading erase visible harm.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 MOTIVE: ACCESS DENIED // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

1. Catch Sentence — Catch the sentence ‘They think…’ or ‘They wanted…’.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Choose Behaviour, you are done.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 BRAID THE SIGNALS // PLAY
Stay with the sequence. You do not need to improve it.

1. Choose Signals — Choose the two signals fighting for attention.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Decide After is your cue to stop.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. Press Equal — Press palms together—or both hands into one cushion—at about twenty percent effort. Keep breathing ordinary.
2. Match Force — Adjust until neither side wins and the pressure feels equal. Hold that match for two seconds.
3. Step Down — Lower both sides together through three gentle levels: fifteen, ten, then five percent.
4. Reach Zero — Reach zero, rest both hands on a stable surface, and notice whether the urge to press returns.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Reach Zero and release the exercise.

Direct data can update the relationship model.

GAME MOVE
Start with Picture Assumption. When Ask Suitable appears, the round is over.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 ASK THE QUESTION FEAR KEEPS ANSWERING // PLAY
Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

1. Picture Assumption — Picture the assumption driving your reaction.
2. Question Whose — Convert it into one clear, non-leading question whose answer could prove the assumption wrong.
3. Ask Suitable — Ask at a suitable time, listen fully, and compare reply plus later behaviour with the original model.

⚡ END MOVE — Ask Suitable. No second lap.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Just before you start Picture Assumption, notice one sound in the room before continuing.
2. At Question Whose, ask, “What would count as evidence against my first answer?”.
3. When you reach Ask Suitable, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Take this line with you: Direct data can update the relationship model.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
At Ask Suitable, you have at least one option the first reaction did not show you.

📸 MY RESULT
“I just separated what was said from what I added to it.”

FORMULA FLOW
Picture Assumption → Question Whose → Ask Suitable

rituals.immediate_need: Ideas, duties, fears, and memories should not share one queue.

GOAL
Ideas, duties, fears, and memories should not share one queue.

GAME MOVE
Open at Question Capture; close at Dont Determine. Keep it light and literal.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 SEPARATE THE MENTAL INBOXES // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Question Capture — Catch each mental item, then route it into IDEA, OBLIGATION, FEAR, MEMORY, or QUESTION.
2. Give Category — Give each category its own processing rule.
3. Dont Determine — Prioritise only after sorting, so emotional intensity does not determine inbox order.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Dont Determine be enough.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 PREVIEW THE AFTER // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Protect Enjoyed — Construct a ten-second scene immediately after completion: what is lighter, available, learned, protected, or enjoyed?
2. Include Sensory — Include a sensory marker plus one practical consequence.
3. State Accessible — Begin the task while that specific after-state remains accessible.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach State Accessible, you are done.

3. When you reach State Accessible, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Delayed reward is undercounted because the mind cannot feel it yet.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 REPLAY THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Recall Exchange — Choose no more than ten seconds of the interaction, beginning before the moment that felt different.
2. Halve Speed — Replay it once in imagination at half speed. Keep to observable words, pauses, volume, face, and movement.
3. Shift — Stop at the first change and name it without motive: ‘the pause lengthened,’ ‘the volume rose,’ or ‘the reply shortened.’
4. Keep Fact — Keep that one fact. End the replay before building another explanation.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Keep Fact be enough.

rituals.name: AUCTION THE NEXT ATTENTION BLOCK
rituals.unique_game_move: Let Let Active begin the game. Let Update Evidence end it.
rituals.recognition_cue: When the fastest response feels like the only response, Auction The Next Attention Block makes the invisible part of the pattern easier to catch.
rituals.situation: When the fastest response feels like the only response, Auction The Next Attention Block makes the invisible part of the pattern easier to catch.
rituals.immediate_need: Limited thought needs a clear way to choose.

TRIGGER
Urgency & decision pressure

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
When the fastest response feels like the only response, Auction The Next Attention Block makes the invisible part of the pattern easier to catch.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Limited thought needs a clear way to choose.

GAME MOVE
Let Let Active begin the game. Let Update Evidence end it.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 AUCTION THE NEXT ATTENTION BLOCK // PLAY
One pass is enough. Follow what is written.

1. Let Active — Let each active concern bid on urgency, consequence, reversibility, and information value.
2. Total — Total the four ratings.
3. Protect Block — Award one protected block to the highest bidder and deny all others entry until time expires.
4. Update Evidence — Re-auction with updated evidence.

⚡ EXIT — Finish Update Evidence and leave the game there.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Give yourself one second before Let Active: soften your jaw and unclench your hands.
2. At Protect Block, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. No Sentences — Imagine five boxes. Do not use full sentences.
2. Imagine Five Signs — Give each of the last five thought turns one simple mental picture.
3. Spot The Return — Notice the first picture whose meaning comes back later.
4. Choose An Exit — At the next box, picture one real fact to check or one small action to take, then stop imagining.

⚡ DONE — Complete Choose An Exit, then return to your day.

🎮 REMEMBER THE FUTURE IN ADVANCE // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

TRIGGER

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Use Interview The Obstacle when your mind keeps delaying the first move. It turns the reaction into a small experiment.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Resistance may be protecting something your plan ignored.

GAME MOVE
Play from Give Obstacle to Picture Negotiate. Treat the last move as the finish line.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE // PLAY
Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

1. Give Obstacle — Give the obstacle a character and ask three questions: What are you protecting?
2. Do — What do you fear will happen?
3. Make Step — What would make one step acceptable?
4. Picture Negotiate — Picture its answers, then negotiate a small action that protects the valid need without handing over total control.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Picture Negotiate and release the exercise.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. To open Give Obstacle, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Make Step, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Picture Negotiate, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Take this line with you: Resistance may be protecting something your plan ignored.

🎮 BORROW ONE MOVE FROM THE AVATAR // PLAY
Stay with the sequence. You do not need to improve it.

1. Create Figure — Create a figure who represents the needed capacity—steady, playful, discerning, brave.

Qualities become accessible when embodied by a character.

Use Create Figure as the doorway and Borrow as the exit.

GOAL

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 WHAT WOULD THIS FACT CHANGE? // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Point Positive — For every desired data point, Picture how a positive, negative, or neutral result would alter the decision.
2. Stop Collecting — If no result changes action, stop collecting it.
3. Prioritise — Prioritise the fact with the largest possible decision swing.

⚡ DONE — Complete Prioritise, then return to your day.

rituals.plain:
WHAT WOULD THIS FACT CHANGE?

TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
What Would This Fact Change? is a tiny mind game for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.

GOAL
Missing information must earn its collection cost.

GAME MOVE
Touch Point Positive, follow the moves, and finish on Prioritise.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 WHAT WOULD THIS FACT CHANGE? // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Point Positive — For every desired data point, Picture how a positive, negative, or neutral result would alter the decision.
2. Stop Collecting — If no result changes action, stop collecting it.
3. Prioritise — Prioritise the fact with the largest possible decision swing.

⚡ DONE — Complete Prioritise, then return to your day.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. At the start of Point Positive, widen your gaze and notice the edges of the room.
2. At Stop Collecting, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Prioritise, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Missing information must earn its collection cost.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
The old reaction loses a little speed before Prioritise.

📸 MY RESULT
“I stopped waiting to feel ready and found one move I could do.”

FORMULA FLOW
Point Positive → Stop Collecting → Prioritise

GOAL
Crowded choices get clearer when only two enter each round.

GAME MOVE
Start at Seed Options. Stop at Crown Next. Let the middle do the work.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Seed Options — Picture the available options into a simple bracket. Give an unpaired option a bye rather than inventing a rival.
2. Pick Criterion — Choose one criterion that matters for this round and Picture it above the bracket. Do not switch it mid-game.
3. Play Pairs — Compare only two options at a time. Advance the one that better meets the declared criterion.
4. Crown Next — Crown the final survivor as the next option to inspect or act on—not as a permanent life verdict.

⚡ FINISH — Crown Next closes the round.

2. At Play Pairs, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Crown Next, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: Crowded choices get clearer when only two enter each round.

rituals.unique_game_move: Start at Hide Already and keep going only until Reveal.
rituals.recognition_cue: The Past Investment Gets No New Vote is for the moment when past effort is pressuring you to keep going—before the reaction gets to choose for you.
rituals.situation: The Past Investment Gets No New Vote is for the moment when past effort is pressuring you to keep going—before the reaction gets to choose for you.

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

HOOK
The Past Investment Gets No New Vote is for the moment when past effort is pressuring you to keep going—before the reaction gets to choose for you.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Sunk cost is history, not future value.

GAME MOVE
Start at Hide Already and keep going only until Reveal.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE PAST INVESTMENT GETS NO NEW VOTE // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Hide Already — Hide what has already been spent.
2. Compare Options — Compare options from today forward using remaining cost, likely benefit, opportunity cost, and risk.
3. Reveal — Reveal the past investment afterward only for learning, never for sharing.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Reveal is your cue to stop.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. As you enter Hide Already, feel where your body is supported for one moment.
2. At Compare Options, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Reveal, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The round ends on this idea: Sunk cost is history, not future value.

GOAL
A rule may fit one situation without ruling your whole life.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE // PLAY
Keep this round small: just the listed moves.

1. Name The Belief — Say the belief silently.
2. Imagine Four Limits — Think about when, where, with whom, and under what conditions it may be true.

items.goal_why_game_move:

Begin where it says Imagine A Pie; stop the moment you complete Choose Repair.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE BLAME PIE // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Imagine A Pie — Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
2. Share The Slices — In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Check The Whole — Make sure all slices together equal 100.
4. Find Your Slice — Focus only on your true share.
5. Choose Repair — Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Choose Repair be enough.

items.unique_game_move: Use Picture as the doorway and Select Direction as the exit.
items.recognition_cue: The Life Direction Test is for the moment when the immediate feeling has pulled you away from what matters—before the reaction gets to choose for you.

items.immediate_need: A thought can sound true and still drive badly.
items.challenge: A thought can sound true and still drive badly.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Values, meaning & loss

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

HOOK
The Life Direction Test is for the moment when the immediate feeling has pulled you away from what matters—before the reaction gets to choose for you.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A thought can sound true and still drive badly.

GAME MOVE
Use Picture as the doorway and Select Direction as the exit.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE LIFE DIRECTION TEST // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Picture — Picture two arrows.
2. Make Room — One shows the next hour if you obey the thought; the other reveals what unfolds over sixty minutes when you make room for it but follow a chosen value.
3. Name Likely — Name the likely behaviour at each arrow’s end.
4. Select Direction — Select by direction, not by mental volume.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Select Direction is your cue to stop.
items.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. As you enter Picture, feel where your body is supported for one moment.
2. At Name Likely, separate responsibility from punishment.
3. When you reach Select Direction, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The round ends on this idea: A thought can sound true and still drive badly.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Close Door — Picture the two leading options. Cross out one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
2. Read Protest — Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Reopen Choice — Uncross the option. Repeat once with the other door closed so both reactions receive the same test.
4. Choose Next — Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.

⚡ END MOVE — Choose Next. No second lap.

🎮 THE CONTROL GRAVEYARD // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Use Control — Name everything used to control the feeling: checking, avoiding, numbing, arguing, reassurance, overworking.
2. Picture Short — Beside each, Picture the short-term payoff and the six-month bill.
3. Focus On Costs — Focus on any method whose bill exceeds its relief.
4. Choose Experiment — Choose one experiment in not paying that cost today.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Choose Experiment be enough.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 MORE THAN THIS STATE // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Carry Qualities — Name three roles you carry, two qualities others have witnessed, and one state present today.
2. Imagine Large — Imagine a large Focus on around all six.
3. Place Painful — Place the current painful content inside, not across, the boundary.
4. Ask Part — Ask which part of the larger system should lead the next action.

⚡ EXIT — Finish Ask Part and leave the game there.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Give yourself one second before Carry Qualities: soften your jaw and unclench your hands.
2. At Place Painful, separate responsibility from punishment.
3. When you reach Ask Part, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The round ends on this idea: A single moment cannot legally seize your whole identity.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You can get from Carry Qualities to Ask Part without adding another story on top.

📸 MY RESULT
“I found where my responsibility ends.”

Carry Qualities → Imagine Large → Place Painful → Ask Part

HOW TO PLAY

One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Review — Review five amplifiers: illness or pain; missed food or hydration; substances or withdrawal; sleep debt; movement deficit or excess.

items.unique_game_move: Begin where it says Drop Define; stop the moment you complete Dont Keep.
items.recognition_cue: Feeling Or Fixing? gives you a quick reset for the moment when your body alarm keeps turning itself up.
items.situation: Feeling Or Fixing? gives you a quick reset for the moment when your body alarm keeps turning itself up.
items.immediate_need: Regulate first; solve only what is solvable.
items.challenge: Regulate first; solve only what is solvable.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Panic & body alarm

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Feeling Or Fixing? gives you a quick reset for the moment when your body alarm keeps turning itself up.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Regulate first; solve only what is solvable.

GAME MOVE
Begin where it says Drop Define; stop the moment you complete Dont Keep.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 FEELING OR FIXING? // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Drop Define — After body alarm drops, define the obstacle without emotional adjectives.
2. Ask Whether — Ask whether a specific action could change it.
3. Choose Action — If yes, choose and schedule that action.
4. Return Acceptance — If no, return to acceptance or support.
5. Dont Keep — Do not keep using soothing when the door requires a key.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Dont Keep be enough.
items.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Right before the first move, Drop Define, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
2. At Choose Action, name the sensation in plain physical words—pressure, heat, tightness, movement.
3. When you reach Dont Keep, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The useful rule here is simple: Regulate first; solve only what is solvable.

📸 MY RESULT
“My body sounded an alarm; I didn't have to turn it into danger.”

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 FINISH THE LOOK // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Let Eyes — Let your eyes move before your head.
2. Scan Left — Slowly scan left, centre, right, behind if safe, and toward an exit.
3. Name Cues — Name present cues of choice, support, and distance from threat.
4. Allow Neck — Allow the neck to follow only within comfort.
5. Place Attention — End by selecting where attention belongs now.

⚡ FINISH — Place Attention closes the round.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 TRACK WHAT HOLDS // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Locate Bodily — Locate one bodily sign of steadiness—warmth, pressure, uprightness, ease, or a capable impulse.
2. Describe Boundaries — Say its boundaries and changes for twenty seconds.
3. Ask Memory — Ask what memory, person, posture, or environment strengthens it by one degree.
4. Add Ingredient — Add only that ingredient.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Add Ingredient, you are done.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 MAP YOUR OPERATING WINDOW // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Imagine Zones — Imagine three zones: TOO HIGH, WORKABLE, TOO LOW.
2. Add Earliest — Add your earliest personal signs in body, speech, attention, and behaviour.
3. Picture Fastest — Beside each outer zone, Picture the fastest safe route toward the middle.
4. Place Others — Place the Imagine a path where others can help recognise it.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Place Others is your cue to stop.

🎮 LET BREATH BREATHE YOU // PLAY

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 BREATHE THE GESTURE // PLAY
Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

1. Choose Slow — Choose one slow movement with two directions—arms open and close, rise and lower, reach and return.
2. Return Direction — Pair the expansive direction with inhale and the returning direction with exhale.
3. Let Movement — Let movement size follow comfort, then complete one cycle without conscious pairing.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Let Movement and release the exercise.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 WHAT SURVIVES THREE STATES? // PLAY
Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

1. Picture Appears — Picture what appears in waking, what appears in dreams, and what is absent or inferred in deep sleep.
2. Ask Claims — Ask which claims of identity remain supported across all three.
3. Hold Conclusions — Hold conclusions lightly; this is an inquiry into ongoing sense, not a demand for belief.

⚡ END MOVE — Hold Conclusions. No second lap.

2. At Ask Claims, ask, “What would count as evidence against my first answer?”.
3. When you reach Hold Conclusions, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Take this line with you: Compare experience across waking, dreaming, and dreamless sleep.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 SAME VALUE, TWO OUTCOMES // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Imagine Action — Imagine the action succeeding.
2. State Governing — State how your governing value behaves next.
3. Imagine Failing — Imagine it failing.
4. State Value — State how the same value responds there.
5. Let Outcome — Let outcome alter strategy, not your ethical centre.

⚡ FINISH — Let Outcome closes the round.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE SUSTAINABLE MIDDLE // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Rest Review — Review sleep, food, effort, practice, and rest.
2. Find Area — Find the area swinging between too much and too little.
3. Set Middle — Set a middle range you could repeat for two weeks.
4. Choose Smallest — Choose the smallest adjustment that moves into that band today.

⚡ EXIT — Finish Choose Smallest and leave the game there.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 EMPTY THE MENTAL COUNTERTOP // PLAY
One pass is enough. Follow what is written.

1. Question Promise — Catch every task, question, promise, and loose obligation into one trusted place.
2. Dont Organise — Do not organise while emptying.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE REQUEST SPINE // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Describe Situation — Say the visible situation.
2. Express Impact — Express its impact.
3. Assert Request — Assert the exact request or no.
4. Reinforce Cooperation — Reinforce why cooperation helps.
5. Picture Sentence — Picture one sentence for each part, then deliver the leanest version.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Picture Sentence be enough.

items.game_move: Begin where it says Describe Situation; stop the moment you complete Picture Sentence.
items.how_to_play:
🎮 THE REQUEST SPINE // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Describe Situation — Say the visible situation.
2. Express Impact — Express its impact.
3. Assert Request — Assert the exact request or no.
4. Reinforce Cooperation — Reinforce why cooperation helps.
5. Picture Sentence — Picture one sentence for each part, then deliver the leanest version.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Picture Sentence be enough.
items.power_up_1: Right before the first move, Describe Situation, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
items.power_up_2: At Assert Request, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
items.power_up_3: When you reach Picture Sentence, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: Clear and firmness needs structure when emotion bends the message.
items.win_reward_raw:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You can complete Picture Sentence without needing perfect certainty first.

📸 MY RESULT
“I found a boundary I could actually say or do.”
items.formula_flow_raw: Describe Situation → Express Impact → Assert Request → Reinforce Cooperation → Picture Sentence

Run the sequence once. Catch Sentence opens it; Choose Behaviour closes it.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 MOTIVE: ACCESS DENIED // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

1. Catch Sentence — Catch the sentence ‘They think…’ or ‘They wanted…’.
2. Replace Possibilities — Replace it with three possibilities and one clear question.
3. Possibility — Notice each possibility as hypothesis, not evidence.
4. Choose Behaviour — Choose behaviour based on what is known while curiosity remains active.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Choose Behaviour, you are done.

items.title: BRAID THE SIGNALS
items.name: BRAID THE SIGNALS
items.unique_game_move: Use Choose Signals as the doorway and Decide After as the exit.
items.recognition_cue: Braid The Signals works best when your mind is stuck on the loudest thing. The goal is not to win an argument with your mind—just change the next move.
items.situation: Braid The Signals works best when your mind is stuck on the loudest thing. The goal is not to win an argument with your mind—just change the next move.
items.immediate_need: Two competing experiences can become one pattern.
items.challenge: Two competing experiences can become one pattern.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Attention & cognitive overload

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
Braid The Signals works best when your mind is stuck on the loudest thing. The goal is not to win an argument with your mind—just change the next move.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Two competing experiences can become one pattern.

GAME MOVE
Use Choose Signals as the doorway and Decide After as the exit.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 BRAID THE SIGNALS // PLAY
Stay with the sequence. You do not need to improve it.

1. Choose Signals — Choose the two signals fighting for attention.
2. Alternate B — Alternate A–B–A–B at a slow fixed rhythm.
3. Hold Time — Then hold both at the same time for one interval, noticing difference without choosing.
4. Decide After — Decide only after the braid is complete.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Decide After is your cue to stop.
items.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. As you enter Choose Signals, feel where your body is supported for one moment.
2. At Hold Time, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Decide After, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Leave the exercise with this: Two competing experiences can become one pattern.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Equal pressure gives restless energy a shared route down.

GAME MOVE
Play from Press Equal to Reach Zero. Treat the last move as the finish line.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. Press Equal — Press palms together—or both hands into one cushion—at about twenty percent effort. Keep breathing ordinary.
2. Match Force — Adjust until neither side wins and the pressure feels equal. Hold that match for two seconds.
3. Step Down — Lower both sides together through three gentle levels: fifteen, ten, then five percent.
4. Reach Zero — Reach zero, rest both hands on a stable surface, and notice whether the urge to press returns.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Reach Zero and release the exercise.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 PREVIEW THE AFTER // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Protect Enjoyed — Construct a ten-second scene immediately after completion: what is lighter, available, learned, protected, or enjoyed?
2. Include Sensory — Include a sensory marker plus one practical consequence.

Abstract distress changes when relationships become physical.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 SCULPT THE PROBLEM // PLAY
One pass is enough. Follow what is written.

1. Use Small — Represent the problem using small objects for people, obstacles, resources, and goals.
2. Feel Arrange — Arrange them as they feel now.
3. Move Object — Move only one object or distance to create a more workable configuration.
4. Name Real — Name the real-life action equivalent to that move.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Name Real is your cue to stop.

items.plain:
SCULPT THE PROBLEM

TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
When your mind keeps delaying the first move, Sculpt The Problem makes the invisible part of the pattern easier to catch.

GOAL
Abstract distress changes when relationships become physical.

GAME MOVE
Start at Use Small and keep going only until Name Real.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 SCULPT THE PROBLEM // PLAY
One pass is enough. Follow what is written.

1. Use Small — Represent the problem using small objects for people, obstacles, resources, and goals.
2. Feel Arrange — Arrange them as they feel now.
3. Move Object — Move only one object or distance to create a more workable configuration.
4. Name Real — Name the real-life action equivalent to that move.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Name Real is your cue to stop.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. As you enter Use Small, feel where your body is supported for one moment.
2. At Move Object, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Name Real, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Let this be the line you keep: Abstract distress changes when relationships become physical.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You reach Name Real without having to solve the entire situation.

📸 MY RESULT
“I stopped waiting to feel ready and found one move I could do.”

FORMULA FLOW
Use Small → Feel Arrange → Move Object → Name Real

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Desired behaviour is easier when it feels feltly familiar.

GAME MOVE
Begin where it says Create Memory; stop the moment you complete Look Backward.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 REMEMBER THE FUTURE IN ADVANCE // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Create Memory — Create a memory-like scene set just after completing the action.
2. Include Time — Include time, location, body posture, one sensory cue, along with what you did when difficulty appeared.
3. Look Backward — Look backward from that imagined completion to the first real movement and perform it now.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Look Backward be enough.
items.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Right before the first move, Create Memory, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
2. At Include Time, name the sensation in plain physical words—pressure, heat, tightness, movement.
3. When you reach Look Backward, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: Desired behaviour is easier when it feels feltly familiar.

items.unique_game_move: Play from Give Obstacle to Picture Negotiate. Treat the last move as the finish line.
items.recognition_cue: Use Interview The Obstacle when your mind keeps delaying the first move. It turns the reaction into a small experiment.

Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Use Interview The Obstacle when your mind keeps delaying the first move. It turns the reaction into a small experiment.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Resistance may be protecting something your plan ignored.

GAME MOVE
Play from Give Obstacle to Picture Negotiate. Treat the last move as the finish line.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE // PLAY
Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

1. Give Obstacle — Give the obstacle a character and ask three questions: What are you protecting?
2. Do — What do you fear will happen?
3. Make Step — What would make one step acceptable?
4. Picture Negotiate — Picture its answers, then negotiate a small action that protects the valid need without handing over total control.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Picture Negotiate and release the exercise.
items.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. To open Give Obstacle, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Make Step, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Picture Negotiate, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Take this line with you: Resistance may be protecting something your plan ignored.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Qualities become accessible when embodied by a character.

GAME MOVE
Use Create Figure as the doorway and Borrow as the exit.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 BORROW ONE MOVE FROM THE AVATAR // PLAY
Stay with the sequence. You do not need to improve it.

1. Create Figure — Create a figure who represents the needed capacity—steady, playful, discerning, brave.
2. Give Posture — Give it posture, voice, and one signature behaviour.
3. Borrow — Borrow only that behaviour for the present situation; there is no need to become the character.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Borrow is your cue to stop.

2. At Give Posture, name the sensation in plain physical words—pressure, heat, tightness, movement.
3. When you reach Borrow, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Leave the exercise with this: Qualities become accessible when embodied by a character.

GOAL
Missing information must earn its collection cost.

GAME MOVE

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 WHAT WOULD THIS FACT CHANGE? // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Point Positive — For every desired data point, Picture how a positive, negative, or neutral result would alter the decision.
2. Stop Collecting — If no result changes action, stop collecting it.
3. Prioritise — Prioritise the fact with the largest possible decision swing.

⚡ DONE — Complete Prioritise, then return to your day.
items.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. At the start of Point Positive, widen your gaze and notice the edges of the room.
2. At Stop Collecting, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.

HOOK
What Would This Fact Change? is a tiny mind game for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.

🎮 WHAT WOULD THIS FACT CHANGE? // PLAY

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Seed Options — Picture the available options into a simple bracket. Give an unpaired option a bye rather than inventing a rival.
2. Pick Criterion — Choose one criterion that matters for this round and Picture it above the bracket. Do not switch it mid-game.
3. Play Pairs — Compare only two options at a time. Advance the one that better meets the declared criterion.
4. Crown Next — Crown the final survivor as the next option to inspect or act on—not as a permanent life verdict.

⚡ FINISH — Crown Next closes the round.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE PAST INVESTMENT GETS NO NEW VOTE // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Hide Already — Hide what has already been spent.
2. Compare Options — Compare options from today forward using remaining cost, likely benefit, opportunity cost, and risk.
3. Reveal — Reveal the past investment afterward only for learning, never for sharing.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Reveal is your cue to stop.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE // PLAY
Keep this round small: just the listed moves.

1. Name The Belief — Say the belief silently.
2. Imagine Four Limits — Think about when, where, with whom, and under what conditions it may be true.
3. Test Inside — Picture one real case where it fits.
4. Test Outside — Picture one real case where it does not fit.
5. Set Its True Place — Say a smaller, more accurate version of the belief.

⚡ DONE — Complete Set Its True Place, then return to your day.

1. At the start of Name The Belief, widen your gaze and notice the edges of the room.
2. At Test Inside, separate responsibility from punishment.
3. When you reach Set Its True Place, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Remember the point: A rule may fit one situation without ruling your whole life.

items.plain:
GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE

TRIGGER
Boundaries & over-responsibility

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
When your responsibility and someone else's have blurred together, try Give The Belief A Postcode. It makes the pattern easier to see and harder to obey.

GOAL
A rule may fit one situation without ruling your whole life.

GAME MOVE
Touch Name The Belief, follow the moves, and finish on Set Its True Place.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE // PLAY
Keep this round small: just the listed moves.

1. Name The Belief — Say the belief silently.
2. Imagine Four Limits — Think about when, where, with whom, and under what conditions it may be true.
3. Test Inside — Picture one real case where it fits.
4. Test Outside — Picture one real case where it does not fit.
5. Set Its True Place — Say a smaller, more accurate version of the belief.

⚡ DONE — Complete Set Its True Place, then return to your day.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. At the start of Name The Belief, widen your gaze and notice the edges of the room.
2. At Test Inside, separate responsibility from punishment.
3. When you reach Set Its True Place, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Remember the point: A rule may fit one situation without ruling your whole life.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
The exercise gives you enough room to make Set Its True Place intentional.

📸 MY RESULT
“I found where my responsibility ends.”

Name The Belief → Imagine Four Limits → Test Inside → Test Outside → Set Its True Place
